user.title: Add a room
user.description: Pick what makes up the room and the scenes to cycle through, in order. A room made of what its scenes set can be anything: a room, a floor, or the whole house. Only scenes made in the scene editor (or scenes.yaml) can be used, because the integration reads what they set the lights to.

data_description.room_scope: Its area's lights: a scene also turns off the area's lights it doesn't set. What its scenes set: a scene only touches what it lists, and the room is off when its off scene matches (or, without one, when everything its scenes switch is off). This can't be changed later.
data_description.area: For a room that's its area's lights: they're this area's lights, with light groups expanded to their members. Not used for a room made of what its scenes set.
data_description.scenes: Next and previous step through these in this order.
data_description.off_scene: Applied to turn the room off. Leave empty to turn off all of the room's lights instead. It can't also be one of the scenes to cycle through.
data_description.include_off: Off comes after a full lap of the scenes, just before the default comes round again. Useful for rooms with a single button. Without wrapping round, off is below the first scene.
data_description.wrap: Next after the last scene goes back to the first. Turn this off for up/down buttons, so the ends stay put: next at the last scene and previous at the first (or at off) apply it again.
data_description.follow_default: When the default changes while the room is showing the old default, switch to the new one straight away. Otherwise a new default only takes effect the next time it's applied.

room.title: Default and lights
room.description: The lights in {area}, apart from any excluded here, make up the room. Room lights that a scene doesn't set are turned off when it's applied, and must be off for the room to count as showing it.

data_description.default_scene: Applied when the room is turned on, and by the first press after the lights were changed outside a scene. Automations can change it.
data_description.excluded_lights: Lights in the area that aren't room lighting, such as indicator LEDs. Ones that look like indicators are suggested.
data_description.brightness_tolerance: How far a light's brightness can be from the scene's and still count as matching.
data_description.position_tolerance: How far a cover's position or tilt can be from the scene's and still count as matching.
data_description.closest_threshold: How different the room can be from a scene (0 = exactly the same, 1 = anything) and still count as closest to it. Shown as the closest_scene attribute.
data_description.manual_next: After the room was changed outside a scene, a press either applies the default, or steps on from the scene the room is closest to (the default if none is close enough).

unreadable_scenes.title: Scene Cycler can't read {room}'s scenes
unreadable_scenes.description:
These scenes either no longer exist or their settings couldn't be read: {scenes}.

If they were deleted or renamed, update the room's options. If they still exist, a Home Assistant update may have changed how scenes are stored, so Scene Cycler needs an update. Until then the room can still cycle, but it can't tell which scene is showing.

next.name: Next scene
next.description: Steps the room to its next scene. From off, or after the lights were changed outside a scene, applies the default.

previous.name: Previous scene
previous.description: Steps the room to its previous scene. From off, or after the lights were changed outside a scene, applies the default.

turn_off.name: Turn off
turn_off.description: Applies the room's off scene, or turns off all its lights if it hasn't got one.
